recommendations.text: For hospitalised, non-ventilated adults within 7 days of ischaemic or haemorrhagic stroke onset, evidence is insufficient to determine whether standardised pneumonia criteria improve clinical outcomes compared with clinician diagnosis alone.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 1; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: In this acute, non-ventilated stroke population, use an algorithm such as PISCES with agreed minimum criteria to diagnose stroke-associated pneumonia (SAP). Observational and secondary trial evidence suggests improved accuracy, but clinical-practice evaluation is needed. Consensus 8/8.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 1; consensus 1

recommendations.text: For non-ventilated adults within 7 days of stroke onset, diagnostic accuracy and clinical-outcome benefit remain uncertain for chest ultrasound or CT compared with chest radiography alone; no evidence-based recommendation can be made.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 2; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Consider chest CT if SAP is suspected but diagnosis is uncertain, particularly when the result could guide antimicrobial or other treatment or exclude alternatives such as pulmonary embolism. Consensus 8/8.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 2; consensus 1

recommendations.text: For non-ventilated adults within 7 days of stroke onset, evidence is insufficient to recommend inflammatory or stress biomarkers for SAP diagnosis.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 3; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Consider adding C-reactive protein to a standardised SAP diagnostic algorithm to improve accuracy in afebrile patients. Available data suggest cut-offs between 30 and 40 mg/L. Consensus 8/8.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 3; consensus 1

recommendations.text: In non-ventilated adults within 7 days of stroke onset, clinical scores and selected biomarkers can identify increased SAP risk with moderate-to-good discrimination. Routine addition of biomarkers to existing scores is not established; usefulness depends on feasible, effective preventive interventions.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 4; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Use validated scores or biomarkers to identify higher-risk patients and target standard SAP-prevention measures. Their limited discrimination constrains current utility; greater value may depend on more effective preventive treatments. Consensus 8/8.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 4; consensus 1

recommendations.section: PICO 5: Scores or biomarkers to guide antibiotics
recommendations.text: For SAP in non-ventilated adults within 7 days of stroke onset, evidence is insufficient to recommend routine prediction scores or biomarkers to guide antibiotic treatment.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 5; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Do not use clinical prediction scores or biomarkers to guide SAP antibiotic treatment on current evidence. Use the guideline's separate recommendations on timing, duration, drug choice and microbiological testing. Consensus 8/8.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 5; consensus 1

recommendations.section: PICO 6: Preventive antibiotics and SAP incidence
recommendations.text: For non-ventilated adults within 7 days of stroke onset, avoid preventive antibiotics to reduce SAP incidence: trials have not shown a reduction in pneumonia.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 6; recommendation 1

recommendations.section: PICO 6: Preventive antibiotics and clinical outcomes
recommendations.text: For non-ventilated adults within 7 days of stroke onset, avoid preventive antibiotics to improve clinical outcomes: benefit has not been demonstrated. The published strength is weak against despite stronger wording in the recommendation sentence.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 6; recommendation 2

recommendations.text: Evidence is insufficient to recommend antiemetics for preventing SAP in non-ventilated adults within 7 days of stroke onset.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 7; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Do not use antiemetics solely to prevent SAP outside clinical trials in acute non-ventilated stroke. They remain appropriate for nausea or vomiting according to local guidance and clinical judgement. The guideline notes an ongoing phase 3 metoclopramide prevention trial at publication. Consensus 8/8.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 7; consensus 1

recommendations.text: No randomised or observational evidence establishes that initiating beta-blockers after stroke prevents pneumonia; no recommendation can be made for this indication in the acute non-ventilated population.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 7; recommendation 2

recommendations.text: Do not initiate beta-blockers solely to prevent SAP within 7 days of stroke. Continue them when already used for another indication: there is no pneumonia-related reason to stop and weak evidence of lower mortality. Consensus 8/8.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 7; consensus 2

recommendations.text: Evidence is insufficient to recommend statins for preventing SAP in non-ventilated adults within 7 days of stroke onset.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 7; recommendation 3

recommendations.text: Do not start a statin specifically to prevent SAP in acute non-ventilated stroke; continue treatment started for another indication. Consensus 8/8.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 7; consensus 3

recommendations.text: Evidence is insufficient to recommend either use or avoidance of ACE inhibitors, ARBs, antacids, proton-pump inhibitors, H2 blockers or benzodiazepines specifically for SAP prevention in acute non-ventilated stroke.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 7; recommendation 4

recommendations.text: Other-indication medicines may affect SAP risk: acid suppression may increase risk, while ACE inhibitors or ARBs in ICH may reduce pneumonia and mortality. Evidence is limited; consider these effects while prescribing strictly for primary indications, such as peptic-ulcer prevention/treatment or hypertension. Consensus 8/8.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 7; consensus 4

recommendations.text: For non-ventilated adults requiring nasogastric feeding within 7 days of stroke, the balance of benefits and harms of intermittent versus continuous feeding remains uncertain.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 8; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: With no clear evidence favouring intermittent or continuous nasogastric feeding, use the mode with which the treating team is most familiar. Consensus 8/8.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 8; consensus 1

recommendations.text: For non-ventilated adults within 7 days of stroke, evidence is insufficient to recommend physical respiratory interventions to prevent SAP or improve clinical outcome.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 9; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Consider respiratory physiotherapy within early post-stroke rehabilitation to prevent SAP. Supporting evidence mainly concerns programmes over several weeks during rehabilitation, often combined with other interventions; two small studies suggest reduced SAP and mortality. Consensus 8/8.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 9; consensus 1

recommendations.text: For non-ventilated adults within 7 days of stroke, begin mobilisation in or out of bed early, within 48 hours, to help prevent SAP.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 10; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Mobilise within 48 hours for SAP prevention, but avoid very early, within 24 hours, prolonged out-of-bed mobilisation in severe stroke because AVERT associated that approach with worse outcomes. Consensus 8/8.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 10; consensus 1

recommendations.text: For non-ventilated adults within 7 days of stroke with reduced consciousness, no clinical evidence establishes whether the recovery position prevents SAP; no evidence-based recommendation can be made.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 11; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: For patients unable to reposition themselves, including those with reduced consciousness, alternate supine and left/right lateral positions every 2 hours during daytime and mobilise passively in bed. Use 30–45° head elevation during and after enteral feeds. Alert patients with mild stroke and no enteral tube may use any comfortable position. Consensus 8/8; turning advice derives from one small study.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 11; consensus 1

recommendations.text: For SAP within 7 days of stroke in non-ventilated adults, effects of >7 versus ≤7 days of antibiotics on clinical outcomes remain uncertain; no evidence-based duration recommendation can be made.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 12; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Tailor SAP antibiotic duration to clinical response; treatment should generally last at least 5 days. Consensus 8/8.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 12; consensus 1

recommendations.text: For SAP within 7 days of stroke in non-ventilated adults, clinical evidence does not establish whether broad-spectrum rather than narrow-spectrum antibiotics improve outcomes.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 13; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: For SAP, follow local or regional aspiration-pneumonia guidance targeting aerobic Gram-negative bacilli and Gram-positive cocci. Dysphagia or confirmed aspiration alone does not justify broader coverage. Include Pseudomonas coverage when relevant risk factors exist. For pneumonia beginning >7 days after stroke, follow local hospital-acquired-pneumonia guidance. Consensus 8/8.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 13; consensus 1

recommendations.text: For SAP within 7 days of stroke in non-ventilated adults, evidence does not establish whether microbiology-directed rather than empiric antibiotics improve clinical outcomes.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 14; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Start empiric SAP antibiotics promptly, ideally within a few hours of clinical diagnosis. When feasible, obtain routine microbiology, such as sputum culture, before antibiotics so subsequent therapy can target an identified pathogen. Consensus 8/8.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 14; consensus 1

recommendations.text: For SAP within 7 days of stroke in non-ventilated adults, clinical-outcome benefits of adjuncts such as cough-assist devices or breathing therapy remain uncertain.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 15; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: An interdisciplinary stroke-unit team may consider cough-assist devices or breathing therapies individually, although these are not standard SAP treatment. Patients with relevant comorbidities, including COPD, may benefit particularly. Consensus 8/8.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 8 images aakag044fx39-1.jpg through aakag044fx39-7.jpg (first panel duplicated); individual PICO boxes aakag044fx4.jpg through aakag044fx38.jpg; PICO 15; consensus 1
